html:
Nanzhao was a kingdom in today's Yunnan in south west China from 738 to 902, with its capital near Erhai Lake at Dali. The 700 map places its shape further south west, along the Burma border.

Its founder, Piluoge, united six small kingdoms with the help of the Tang dynasty in 738. Within a few years Nanzhao turned on its patron. Allied with the Tibetan Empire, it destroyed two large Tang armies in the 750s, just before the An Lushan rebellion shook China. In 794 it switched sides again and joined the Tang against Tibet.

Nanzhao was a strong military state. It raided Sichuan, sacking Chengdu in 829, and attacked the Pyu city-states in Burma and the Tang province in today's northern Vietnam. A minister seized the throne in 902, and after years of turmoil the Dali Kingdom took its place in 937.
